hook: 45 seconds. That's all it took for one AI agent to link 586 pages while Claude Opus barely finished 21.
caption:
Same 586 pages, same clock: TypeSafe AI's Jev finished the whole internal link map in 45.1 seconds for $0.21, placing 584 links and skipping 139 pages that genuinely didn't fit.

Claude Opus 5 got through 21 pages in that time for $1.43, about 190x more per page. The full pass would have cost $43.

Internal linking is really 8,790 yes/no calls, not writing, which is exactly what a fast decision model is built for.
checked: Jev (TypeSafe AI System One model), founder ex-OpenAI, and the 586-page/45.1s/$0.21 vs. Claude Opus 5 21-page/$1.43 internal-linking demo: https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/jev-for-seo
Claude Opus 5 is a real, current Anthropic model, priced $5/$25 per million tokens: https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5

captions.instagram:
45 seconds. That's all it took for one AI agent to rebuild an entire site's internal link map 🤯

TypeSafe AI's Jev read all 586 pages, placed 584 links, and skipped 139 pages that genuinely didn't fit, all for $0.21.

Claude Opus 5, same pages, same clock, only got through 21 of them for $1.43. About 190x more per page.

Internal linking isn't really writing, it's thousands of yes/no calls: does this page have a real reason to link to that one? That's a job built for a fast decision model, not a frontier LLM.
